pillars.bodyMarkdown:
Astrid is designed to support serious, sustained artistic practice.

Everything should be built so that artists can define, direct, and understand their work. From early experimentation through sustained projects to finished pieces, Astrid should foster a deep, evolving partnership between the artist, their agents, and their tools—one that expands possibility while preserving the artist's intent and judgment.

## Aspirations

### Artistic agency

Astrid should be designed so artists can define and direct their work at every stage.

The creator chooses what to make, how to refine it, and which advice to accept. Their agents and tools should become ever more capable collaborators without silently replacing artistic judgment or making decisions impossible to inspect and understand.

### Continuity and iteration

Ambitious work should remain editable across many sessions and revisions.

A project must preserve its materials, decisions, history, and working state so that artists can return, compare alternatives, refine difficult passages, and sustain a coherent direction over time. Continuity is what allows the artist's relationship with their tools and agents to deepen rather than reset with every session.

### Finished artistic work

The tool should help creators carry their ideas through to meaningful completed work.

Every blocker that inhibits artists from making original, demanding pieces is worth tackling, whether it is a small irritation or a fundamental limit of the technology. No problem should be beneath our attention or beyond our ambition in that pursuit; we should judge success by the finished work artists can make and stand behind.

## References

**Gap:** [AA-001 — Sustained, ambitious creative work](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/vision/gaps/AA-001-sustained-creative-work.md). The [guiding principles](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/vision/README.md#four-driving-principles) apply here too.

characteristics.title: A small, dependable foundation
characteristics.summary: The shared core should stay understandable and reliable while creative tools evolve around it.
characteristics.detailsMarkdown:

The same authoritative operations are available to people and agents through interchangeable interfaces, whether the workspace lives on their own machine or in the cloud. New creative tools and modalities build on explicit shared contracts; they do not need to depend on or fork the core's implementation. A dependable core enables, rather than constrains, live experimentation above it.

characteristics.title: Live tool composition
characteristics.summary: Creators and agents should be able to reshape their tools without interrupting creative work.
characteristics.detailsMarkdown: Every interface component should be dockable, floatable, nestable, or spatially arrangeable, while keeping its bindings to the right timeline, selection, playback, and task. Agents should be equally free to reorganize and extend their own tools to accomplish a creative goal, within the creator's permissions. Neither a human nor an agent should lose project state simply because a tool has been rearranged. People should be able to ask their agents to open a specific creative resource, show the right tool, arrange and connect views and restore the previous workspace through the same supported operations as a human, with explicit target and bindings and without having to rewrite the interface for ordinary changes.

characteristics.title: Real-time functionality
characteristics.summary: The capabilities of a tool should be adjustable while the creator is using it.
characteristics.detailsMarkdown: People and agents should be able to connect components, change behavior, introduce controls, and install trusted extensions as the creative problem changes. An agent should also be able to extend its own capabilities rather than remain trapped by a fixed initial toolset. Every extension should expose useful ways for others to build on it. People and agents should be able to change existing creative interfaces, write complete new tools and substitute compatible views while retaining their work, using the same supported extension contracts as Astrid's default creative tools. Ordinary extensions should not require rebuilding the shared core; a failed extension should not strand the creator or prevent recovery.

characteristics.title: Opinionated tools, not extra scaffolding
characteristics.summary: A good ready-made tool should remain useful without requiring its creator to customize it.
characteristics.detailsMarkdown: Creators can work with a considered default composition or adapt every layer as needed. Existing components should be reused before inventing another framework; 2D workspaces and spatial experiences should share primitives without making either mandatory.

characteristics.title: Packs are live, portable and extensible
characteristics.summary: A pack should be something you can change while you are using it and take anywhere Astrid runs.
characteristics.detailsMarkdown:
A pack is a living part of the workspace, not a separate development project that interrupts making art. People and agents can find, adapt and combine its capabilities while they work. One extension contract connects the interface and Python backend, so a useful contribution can be shared, installed and extended without becoming tied to its author's setup. The contract is open to other implementation languages too. An independently built tool can use the same authoritative resources and be selected instead of a default interface without a core fork or project migration; permissions, versioning and recovery still apply.

A creative contribution should be able to introduce its own durable data model and evolve it as creative needs change. Its data should remain usable, portable and recoverable across tool updates, removal, reinstall and local or hosted work, without changing the shared foundation or accessing another contribution's private data. Astrid should handle the infrastructure of data ownership, permissions, migration and recovery so a contributor can concentrate on the tool's creative meaning.

**We should:**

- Render a pack's changes in the running app at once, including the web app.
- Let a creator or agent vibe-code a pack while working in it.
- Make one pack run unchanged on any install.
- Let a pack extend another pack from inside it.
- Give one defined way to build an extension that covers the front end and the Python back end together.

**We should never:**

- Require a rebuild or restart to see a pack change.
- Tie a pack to one machine or one install.
- Add a second way to write an extension for one side only.
- Build a feature that only works because it bypasses the pack contract.

pillars.bodyMarkdown:
Tools should adapt to creative work as people and agents create together.

“We shape our tools, and thereafter our tools shape us” is a philosophy we should leave in the twentieth century. Astrid is a shared foundation for open, composable creative tools. Their composition and functionality should be adjustable in real time, while people and agents are working. Removing the friction of reshaping software is essential to expanding what we can create, individually and together.

## Aspirations

### A small, dependable foundation

The shared core should stay understandable and reliable while creative tools evolve around it.

Timelines, media, projects, identities, validated operations, and permissions are durable resources shared by human-facing interfaces and agents. Specialized behavior belongs in reusable components and packs; extend the core only for genuinely shared needs.

The foundation should be fast, independently operable and recoverable: it can inspect, preserve and repair creative work even when an interface, agent provider or managed creative environment fails. The same authoritative operations are available to people and agents through interchangeable interfaces, whether the workspace lives on their own machine or in the cloud. New creative tools and modalities build on explicit shared contracts; they do not need to depend on or fork the core's implementation. A dependable core enables, rather than constrains, live experimentation above it.

### Live tool composition

Creators and agents should be able to reshape their tools without interrupting creative work.

Every interface component should be dockable, floatable, nestable, or spatially arrangeable, while keeping its bindings to the right timeline, selection, playback, and task. Agents should be equally free to reorganize and extend their own tools to accomplish a creative goal, within the creator's permissions. Neither a human nor an agent should lose project state simply because a tool has been rearranged. People should be able to ask their agents to open a specific creative resource, show the right tool, arrange and connect views and restore the previous workspace through the same supported operations as a human, with explicit target and bindings and without having to rewrite the interface for ordinary changes.

### Real-time functionality

The capabilities of a tool should be adjustable while the creator is using it.

People and agents should be able to connect components, change behavior, introduce controls, and install trusted extensions as the creative problem changes. An agent should also be able to extend its own capabilities rather than remain trapped by a fixed initial toolset. Every extension should expose useful ways for others to build on it. People and agents should be able to change existing creative interfaces, write complete new tools and substitute compatible views while retaining their work, using the same supported extension contracts as Astrid's default creative tools. Ordinary extensions should not require rebuilding the shared core; a failed extension should not strand the creator or prevent recovery.

### Shared human–agent work

People and agents should act on the same authoritative creative resources.

A pack can provide agent actions and human-facing interfaces around the same timeline or project. Both should observe permissions, avoid overwriting one another's changes, and allow creators to understand and reverse consequential operations.

### Opinionated tools, not extra scaffolding

A good ready-made tool should remain useful without requiring its creator to customize it.

Creators can work with a considered default composition or adapt every layer as needed. Existing components should be reused before inventing another framework; 2D workspaces and spatial experiences should share primitives without making either mandatory.

### Packs are live, portable and extensible

A pack should be something you can change while you are using it and take anywhere Astrid runs.

A pack is a living part of the workspace, not a separate development project that interrupts making art. People and agents can find, adapt and combine its capabilities while they work. One extension contract connects the interface and Python backend, so a useful contribution can be shared, installed and extended without becoming tied to its author's setup. The contract is open to other implementation languages too. An independently built tool can use the same authoritative resources and be selected instead of a default interface without a core fork or project migration; permissions, versioning and recovery still apply.

A creative contribution should be able to introduce its own durable data model and evolve it as creative needs change. Its data should remain usable, portable and recoverable across tool updates, removal, reinstall and local or hosted work, without changing the shared foundation or accessing another contribution's private data. Astrid should handle the infrastructure of data ownership, permissions, migration and recovery so a contributor can concentrate on the tool's creative meaning.

**We should:**

- Render a pack's changes in the running app at once, including the web app.
- Let a creator or agent vibe-code a pack while working in it.
- Make one pack run unchanged on any install.
- Let a pack extend another pack from inside it.
- Give one defined way to build an extension that covers the front end and the Python back end together.

**We should never:**

- Require a rebuild or restart to see a pack change.
- Tie a pack to one machine or one install.
- Add a second way to write an extension for one side only.
- Build a feature that only works because it bypasses the pack contract.

## Aspirations

### An ecosystem of wisdom grounded in real work

Creative experience should become useful, testable knowledge that others can build on.

Before acting, an agent can look for applicable prior experience. During work it distinguishes evidence from assumptions; afterward it retains reusable lessons with relevant conditions, source versions, failures, and counterexamples.

### Use knowledge with judgment

Shared knowledge should be evaluated rather than treated as unquestionable instruction.

A finding may depend on a particular model, creative task, environment, or source revision. Agents must check that it still applies and preserve disagreements, uncertainty, and stale evidence when making decisions.

### Share without surrendering control

Creators should decide which discoveries stay private and which can help others.

Local, team, and community knowledge remain under their respective owners' authority. Useful findings can flow between them with attribution, permission, and the ability to withhold or revoke access.

pillars.bodyMarkdown:
We want to create the conditions for the community to do more together.

We want a collective that inspires people to attempt more demanding artistic and technical work, helping them grow through collaboration and critique. We also want to reward meaningful contributions by sharing ownership in the company with people who advance our core product and wider ecosystem. An Astrid-centered culture and a legally workable ownership model still need to be established.

## Aspirations

### Shared challenges and ambition

Challenges and collaborations should encourage artists to attempt work beyond their previous limits.

Competitions and collective projects should be designed around artistic intent, fair participation, completed work, and learning—not simply attention or participation metrics.

### Critique and mutual growth

Creators should be able to learn from one another's practice and judgment.

Mentorship, thoughtful feedback, shared techniques, and recognition of exceptional work should build confidence and capability across the community, including for people approaching unfamiliar media or tools.

### A meaningful stake in the collective

Contributors should have a genuine opportunity to benefit from advancing the shared mission.

The stated ambition includes ownership in the company behind the collective for people who advance its mission. Eligibility, allocation, governance, financing, and legal and tax implementation remain unresolved; this vision does not grant equity or promise a particular allocation.

### Many hands, one clear way in

Any person or agent should be able to pick up useful work and land it without getting in anyone else's way.

The shared vision should lead to work that a contributor can understand, claim, improve and prove. Clear ownership and a visible trail of decisions help parallel efforts meet without duplicating work or hiding what remains unfinished. The process should make contribution easier, not become a second project that people must master before they can help.

Run fully locally, or cheaply and conveniently in the cloud.

Astrid should be built so that creative work can happen entirely on your machine, even offline, with your projects and files under your control. The same work should be convenient and inexpensive to run in the cloud when helpful. People and their agents should choose where work happens, what is shared, and what it costs.

## Aspirations

### Local work as the default

Creators should be able to make and preserve work on their own computers.

The local project should remain authoritative when the creator chooses a local-first workflow. They can inspect, reopen, revise, and retain the underlying files without depending on a permanent cloud connection.

### Everything local or cloud, by choice

Everything should be able to run locally, and nothing should have to.

Local capability gives creators custody without making ownership of a particular computer a condition of participation. A creator can choose a fully local workspace, selected remote capabilities or a fully hosted workspace. That choice remains explicit and reversible, with work able to return to the creator's own machine rather than becoming trapped in a service.

**We should:**

- Make every capability work fully on the creator's own machine.
- Let a creator run the whole workspace in the cloud if they choose.
- Let work move back into the creator's custody.

**We should never:**

- Ship a capability that only works in the cloud.
- Require a local machine to use Astrid.
- Move work to the cloud without the creator choosing it.

### Clear boundaries and costs

The creator should know where work runs and what leaves their machine.

Choices about uploaded data, remote storage, permissions, services, and costs should be visible and revocable where possible, so convenience does not obscure control.

### Cloud as frugal as possible

Cloud tools should be inexpensive enough to encourage experimentation rather than ration it.

Artists have always shared tips on where to find affordable materials—even cheap turpentine matters when you need the freedom to try things. We want the same spirit in cloud inference: use efficient models and infrastructure, make costs easy to compare, and seek the least expensive suitable route to a creative result. Frugality should broaden experimentation without sacrificing quality, privacy, or the creator's choices.

principles.bodyMarkdown:
We aim to share our code, knowledge, ideas and ownership.

Our code is open, but openness should reach further: to our evolving vision, experiments, decisions, execution, and what remains unfinished. Knowledge and ideas should be reusable, with creators deciding what private work they share. We also aspire to share company ownership with meaningful contributors; the eligibility, allocation, and legal implementation of that commitment are not yet settled.

## Aspirations

### Inspectable foundations

Anyone should be able to trace how the tools they depend on actually work.

Source code, models, interfaces, tests, and documented behavior should make it possible to investigate how a tool works, where its limitations lie, and which decisions shaped it. Openness should extend to the reasoning behind our technical and strategic choices, not just the resulting artifacts.

### Forking must be real

The right to adapt a tool should be practical, not merely a line in a license.

Creators should be able to inspect, copy, modify, replace, and independently maintain the components they depend on, within the rights of their licenses. Portable projects, understandable interfaces, and replaceable providers make the freedom to fork a real option rather than a theoretical promise.

### Built to be found and reused

People and agents should be able to find, understand, adapt and build on each other's contributions.

Publishing source is only the beginning of reuse. Packs, tools, workflows and knowledge need enough context to be discovered, judged and put to work by someone who did not create them. Their interfaces, dependencies, provenance and terms should remain inspectable, so sharing can lead to new creative work rather than a collection of opaque artifacts.

### Open decisions and working knowledge

We should share how things really work, not only the code that implements them.

With the creator's permission, useful workflows, agent discoveries, failures, model choices, and knowledge from actual projects should be shareable with attribution and context. We should openly explain the relationship between our vision, experiments, implementation, results, and remaining gaps; we have not made that relationship sufficiently clear yet. Private material and sensitive information stay under their owners' control.

## References

Related work is tracked in the [vision gap catalog](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/tree/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/vision/gaps), including [CA-003 — Public vision and progress are not yet clearly connected](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/vision/gaps/CA-003-vision-experiments-progress.md) and [CA-002 — Contributor ownership](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/vision/gaps/CA-002-contributor-ownership.md).

Creators have the final say over their creative environments.

Astrid should make it possible to choose features and services, control agent permissions, and decide what stays private or becomes shared. Even core workings should be adaptable, without requiring artists to become experts in the underlying technology.

## Aspirations

### Control at every layer

Creators should be able to change the capabilities they rely on.

They can choose, inspect, replace, or extend features and services, including fundamental parts of the environment, while keeping the work and its history understandable.

### Explicit permissions and privacy

Agents should act within boundaries the creator can understand and change.

Access to files, networks, services, and spending must be scoped and inspectable. Creators should be able to deny or revoke permissions and decide what information is retained or shared.

### Approachable, reversible choices

Control should be easy to exercise without technical expertise.

Interfaces should show the meaningful consequences of decisions, support correction and recovery, and make it possible to undo or refuse risky changes rather than treating control as an advanced setting.

characteristics.title: One generation path, any engine, any machine
characteristics.summary: Every generation should run the same way wherever it runs and whatever runs it.
characteristics.detailsMarkdown:
Start with the request and its requirements, choose a destination once, bring it into line when necessary, run on the chosen engine and return the result. Creators can set a default destination and override it for a generation. Workflows, engines and machines are independently replaceable pieces: adding one should reuse everything on the other side of its contract, rather than require another route through the core.

**We should:**

- Send every generation, in every modality, through one path.
- Make the engine a choice on that path: a cloud service, ComfyUI, Wan2GP or another inference engine.
- Make the machine a separate choice: this computer, your own server or a rented GPU.
- Let a new engine or machine plug in by meeting a declared contract, then work with everything on the other side.

**We should never:**

- Add a route for one modality or one pack just for now.
- Build an engine so that it only works with one kind of machine.
- Hide from the creator where a generation runs.
- Build our own inference engine.

- Send every generation, in every modality, through one path.
- Make the engine a choice on that path: a cloud service, ComfyUI, Wan2GP or another inference engine.
- Make the machine a separate choice: this computer, your own server or a rented GPU.
- Let a new engine or machine plug in by meeting a declared contract, then work with everything on the other side.

- Add a route for one modality or one pack just for now.

gaps.title: Astrid hasn't yet proven it can sustain ambitious work end to end
gaps.assessmentDetail: Open, initial source assessment (2026-11-06); not a live product qualification.
gaps.desiredMarkdown: A person can pursue a substantial, distinctive creative vision from early exploration through deep iteration to finished work, retaining control of their artistic decisions and improving their craft.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Astrid provides a video editor, generation capabilities, agent-led timeline editing and creative packs. These are substantial foundations, but **we haven't yet demonstrated that Astrid can sustain a demanding, creator-led artistic project from exploration through deep revisions to a finished work**. The limits of artistic control, continuity and quality over a long project remain unproven.
gaps.missingMarkdown: The ceiling on sustained artistic control, continuity, revision and creative quality is not yet established through an ambitious end-to-end project.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: A real artist-led project is completed through repeated revision, with demonstrable continuity, editable results, preserved creative intent and serious creator/peer assessment. Record what the tools enabled, where they constrained ambition and what remains unresolved.

gaps.title: Astrid doesn't yet have a culture where creatives thrive
gaps.assessmentDetail: Open; prior Banodoco competitions, but no established Astrid-specific program/outcome audit.
gaps.desiredMarkdown: People have compelling reasons to attempt work beyond their current abilities: artistic challenges, collaboration, critiques, showcases and high standards that encourage originality and growth.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Astrid builds on the existing Banodoco community, which has run art competitions including the [Arca Gidan Prize](https://arcagidan.com/). But **Astrid has not yet established a community centred on this tool and its artistic mission**, with a repeatable culture of challenges, critique and collective artistic growth. Earlier competitions provide experience and a starting point, not evidence that this new culture already exists.
gaps.missingMarkdown: Astrid doesn't yet have a thriving culture of creatives challenging, inspiring and helping one another reach beyond their current abilities. Challenges, critique, showcases and recognition should be judged by the creative work and growth they enable, not activity counts alone.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: Run a bounded challenge with clear artistic intent and fair participation; document artists' goals, feedback, completed work and whether it enabled more ambitious efforts. Incorporate genuine creator assessment, including negative findings and barriers.

gaps.title: No implemented contributor-ownership model
gaps.assessmentDetail: Open; earlier Banodoco arrangement lapsed, Astrid model and legal terms not established.
gaps.desiredMarkdown: The people who meaningfully advance the collective have a genuine, understandable stake in the company behind it. The stated ambition is **100% ownership for contributors advancing the mission**, not merely participation rewards.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Banodoco published a contributor-ownership approach, monthly grant lists and reported transfers. Its earlier proposal described splitting 1% per month over 8.5 years, with changing contributor categories and an explicitly provisional legal structure. The program has not been actively maintained during Astrid's recent development. **The historical publications are evidence of earlier commitments, not proof of legally issued equity.** An Astrid-specific arrangement must reconcile those records and existing promises before deciding new eligibility, allocation, governance, financing or implementation.
gaps.missingMarkdown: A transparent and legally workable mechanism for translating meaningful contributions—creative, technical, mentoring or otherwise—into ownership and rights, including treatment of existing and future financing, has not yet been specified or implemented.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: An explicit owner decision and qualified legal/tax review of a concrete model covering eligible contributions, grants/allocations, governance, vesting, changes over time, financing and participant protections; then evidence of its authorized implementation. A declaration alone does not close this gap.

gaps.title: Our vision and execution aren't yet fully connected
gaps.assessmentDetail: Partially evidenced (2026-11-09; public vision, gaps and project summaries exist, but their relationship to experiments and execution has not been demonstrated end to end).
gaps.desiredMarkdown: Someone outside the core team can understand what Astrid is trying to achieve, why particular experiments or projects were undertaken, what was actually tried, what the evidence showed, what decisions changed, and which gaps remain. This trail should be accessible, candid about failed or abandoned approaches, and kept current as work develops.
gaps.currentMarkdown: We've been revamping [astrid-dev](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/README.md) and the [public Astrid Vision page](https://astrid.haus/vision) to connect pillars and principles to real gaps and projects. Those are meaningful pieces of transparency, but they still don't demonstrate a consistently maintained, readable chain from ambition through experiments and implementation to evidence, outcomes and changed plans. Existing public documents are a start, not proof that someone can reliably follow that reasoning.
gaps.missingMarkdown: We have not communicated our vision, the experiments exploring it, actual execution, and the gaps between intention and reality well enough as one connected story. Unlike [CA-001](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/vision/gaps/CA-001-creative-challenge-culture.md), this is about public understanding and accountability, not establishing challenges or artistic participation; unlike [CA-002](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/vision/gaps/CA-002-contributor-ownership.md), it is not about legally implementing contributor ownership.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown:
Publish a maintained public trail for at least three substantive decisions or experiments, each connecting the relevant vision and gap to the hypothesis, work attempted, evidence, outcome, resulting decision, and what remains unresolved.

Include at least one negative, abandoned, or changed approach without presenting it as success; verify the source links and revisions. Have independent contributors unfamiliar with those efforts locate the rationale and current outcome, record where they were confused, and demonstrate that resulting improvements make the chain understandable. Reassess after subsequent substantive work rather than only at the initial publication.

gaps.title: Creators and agents can't yet find one another's contributions
gaps.assessmentDetail: Open; initial assessment (2026-11-10); not implementation proof.
gaps.desiredMarkdown: Creators and agents can discover other people's packs, creative components, skills and reusable work in one coherent place, evaluate relevance, provenance, licensing, maintenance and compatibility, and reuse what is appropriate.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Astrid has agent pack manifests and an emerging [Hivemind](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/plans/22-hivemind-protocol/plan.md), but there is no proven streamlined discovery experience across contributors. Community search and individual links are not the same as a reliable, task-aware index for both people and agents.
gaps.missingMarkdown: No dependable discovery, indexing, provenance and compatibility path for published creative contributions exists yet. This is distinct from [F-004](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/vision/gaps/F-004-pack-lifecycle.md), which concerns installing/updating a known pack, and [CI-003](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/vision/gaps/CI-003-public-source-ingestion.md), which concerns intake of external public knowledge.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: An independent contributor publishes a versioned contribution; a creator and an agent separately discover it through relevant search, inspect identity, source, compatibility and trust signals, then follow a supported reuse path. Demonstrate stale, removed, incompatible and untrusted results without automatic install or unauthorized sharing.

gaps.title: Many contributors and agents can't yet work in parallel through one clear process
gaps.assessmentDetail: Open / partly evidenced (2026-11-12): Plan 48's committed scope is complete and shown on astrid-dev's `main` and in a scratch repository, and Plan 51 finished its two parts (route step 2); none of it is from observed work at scale.
gaps.desiredMarkdown: Someone new, or their agent, can learn from one place each what kinds of record Astrid's development workspace keeps, what is checked and when, which pages are written by hand and which are generated, and how to extend any of them. Many people and agents can then propose, claim, progress and finish projects at the same time without waiting on, or overwriting, one another.
gaps.currentMarkdown:
The contribution principles, skills, templates and checks exist and a small number of contributors use them daily. As read on 11 Nov 2026 ([findings](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/plans/48-one-record-model/inputs.md#what-exists-today)): there is no list of what is checked; local and CI runs can disagree; one generated-page pipeline exists and is not reusable; several facts have two hand-kept homes; every change to any project's owner, standing or estimate edits one shared table; ten of 47 project plans follow the template; and two projects share a number. This shows structure only. Nothing here has been observed with many contributors working at once.

**After Plan 51 (12 Nov 2026):** each rule is written in one place and each role and unit of work is defined once, in a glossary; one skill says where a change to astrid-dev goes and how to prove it; the skills and contributor docs hold fewer words than at the project's start (29,410 to 29,181 at its last merge), and the scripts fewer lines (3,005 to 2,996). One fresh worker, given the new skill and the extending guide, added a check; its confusions were recorded, and seven were fixed in the skill and the guide. That is one worker on one task. A new generated page was not tried, and nothing was run with many contributors at once.
gaps.missingMarkdown: The workspace's structure is carried by prose and by separate scripts, so it is hard to learn, hard to extend in one place, and it funnels unrelated work through shared files. Unlike [CA-003](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/vision/gaps/CA-003-vision-experiments-progress.md), this is about people being able to work through the process together, not about the public following why work happened; unlike [CA-004](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/vision/gaps/CA-004-sharing-and-discovery.md), it concerns contributing to Astrid's development, not finding published creative contributions.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown:
- One command lists every check and every generated page, and gives the same result locally and in CI.
- A new project lands by adding only its own folder. Ten contributors adding or updating different projects from the same starting point all merge without conflict.
- Each kind of fact has one source. Asked where to change five different facts, a fresh contributor finds each single source from the documentation.
- A fresh agent adds a check and a generated page from the extension guide alone; its confusions are recorded and resolved.
- Refusals work: a hand edit to a generated page, a claim made for someone else, and a project marked finished without its completion form are each rejected.
- Reassessed after a real period in which at least ten contributors worked at the same time, with the process stalls of that period recorded.

gaps.title: Agents don't yet reliably learn from creative work
gaps.assessmentDetail: Open, source assessment (2026-11-06).
gaps.desiredMarkdown: An agent routinely uses applicable earlier lessons **before** work, captures truthfully observed success or failure **during/after** work, learns within a user-owned private knowledge scope and can propose sanitized contributions to others with explicit permission.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Astrid Agent has executable creative tools and Runtime task/artifact records. Banodoco Hivemind has an evidence-bearing read/contribution system. The [source map](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/plans/22-hivemind-protocol/inputs.md) **does not establish a complete private/local → community → later-agent learning loop**.
gaps.missingMarkdown: Contextual retrieval, actual run-to-knowledge capture, safe private retention, consented contributions and proven benefits to a second agent session are not yet integrated end to end.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: Two real agent sessions: the first retrieves applicable knowledge and produces an observed, locally retained result; a subsequent session demonstrably uses that finding. Optional contribution retains provenance and only shares approved, sanitized information. Compare against raw search/no knowledge, including staleness and denial paths.

gaps.title: Hivemind functionality isn't yet refined and interoperable
gaps.assessmentDetail: Open, proposal compared with source (2026-11-06).
gaps.desiredMarkdown: Independent personal, team and community knowledge datasets can preserve attribution, conditions, evidence and owner-controlled access while exchanging permitted references and learnings without merging into one central authority.
gaps.currentMarkdown: [Banodoco Hivemind](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/plans/22-hivemind-protocol/inputs.md) documents source-custodied messages, revisioned resources, an accepted search head and editorial contribution operations. The [uploaded October 29 protocol proposal](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/plans/22-hivemind-protocol/protocol-proposal.md) proposes dataset-scoped entries, typed links and `find`/`inspect`/`contribute`. **These are not yet identical proven contracts.**
gaps.missingMarkdown: Hivemind's existing functionality and proposed protocol still need refinement and real proof: stable versioned identities, useful references, access decisions and scoped exchange between independently owned datasets. Public-source ingestion belongs to [CI-003](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/vision/gaps/CI-003-public-source-ingestion.md), rather than being rolled into this gap.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: Two separately owned datasets can exchange a scoped, independently attributed reference or approved sanitized result, preserving revision identity, provenance and access decisions; denied, stale and revoked cases do not leak source content. Banodoco behavior is preserved or safely, explicitly migrated with evidence.

gaps.title: Hivemind doesn't yet learn from public internet resources
gaps.assessmentDetail: Open; initial assessment (2026-11-10); not implementation proof.
gaps.desiredMarkdown: Hivemind can help agents retrieve relevant knowledge from public GitHub issues and discussions, Reddit, technical documentation and other permitted sources, with attribution, version history, freshness and critical assessment.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Current [Hivemind source work](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/plans/22-hivemind-protocol/inputs.md) does not establish a maintained cross-source ingestion and freshness pipeline. A proposed federation protocol and community contributions are not proof of wider public knowledge intake.
gaps.missingMarkdown: Rights-aware source connectors, revision tracking, deduplication, removals, freshness signals and source-grounded retrieval are not yet demonstrated. This is distinct from independent Hivemind federation ([CI-002](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/vision/gaps/CI-002-federated-knowledge.md)) and learning from Astrid work ([CI-001](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/vision/gaps/CI-001-agent-learning-loop.md)).
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: Ingest an authorized sample of GitHub issues/discussions, Reddit posts and documentation with source identity and revisions. A real agent retrieves and critically uses relevant evidence. Show updates, conflicting claims, rate limits, removals, permission failures and prompt injection never becoming action authority.

gaps.title: Reliability isn't proven across supported setups
gaps.assessmentDetail: Partially evidenced (2026-11-06; source is existing plan/queue evidence, not a new qualification).
gaps.desiredMarkdown: On each declared supported operating system, device and deployment route, people can reliably install, launch, stop, update, roll back, repair and remove Astrid without losing projects or becoming stranded in an unexplained state. This concerns the application's **operational lifecycle**, not whether every creative workflow succeeds.
gaps.currentMarkdown:
[Plan 29](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/plans/29-update-and-release/plan.md) is reopened: Release 10 (0.0.10) is published, but `install --update` on a machine that already completed the Release 1 storage handoff exits 0 and installs nothing. Less common setups remain in [Plan 30](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/plans/30-update-everywhere/plan.md).


[Plan 08](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/plans/08-release1-install-update/plan.md) records a completed five-row hosted R1 installation/update gate, proving that *specific* paths worked on *specific* candidates. The [project queue](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/README.md) records Plan 07 as active with indicative Pinokio evidence and existing CI failures, while Plans 09/10 target broader routes and native qualification. This is **not** proof that all devices, browser variants or real engines are covered.
gaps.missingMarkdown: Supported installation, launcher and engine lifecycle transitions—especially updates, failures, rollback, cleanup and recovery—still lack sufficiently broad, current and reproducible qualification. Creative job correctness belongs to F-003; authority over agent actions belongs to F-002.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: A declared and version-pinned OS/device/deployment matrix demonstrates clean installation, launch, stop, update, interruption recovery, rollback and removal with preserved work and meaningful negative tests. This qualifies supported operational paths, not creative inference accuracy or permission policy.

gaps.title: User control and recovery aren't fully proven
gaps.assessmentDetail: Open / partly implemented foundations (2026-11-06).
gaps.desiredMarkdown: People can understand, grant, limit and revoke what Astrid and its agents may access, change, share or spend, and can recover safely from conflicting or rejected actions. Consequential changes, external effects and resource use follow explicit authority, and a refusal is respected. A sandbox is one safeguard, not the whole definition of creator control.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Astrid Runtime has versioned project/task authority and the App/Agent have meaningful editing and conflict primitives. [Plan 01](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/plans/01-installer-consent/plan.md) is for installer choice; [Plan 04](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/plans/04-concurrent-edits/plan.md) addresses concurrent edits; [Plan 15](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/plans/15-openshell-safe-execution/plan.md) targets the independent [F-007 sandbox outcome](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/vision/gaps/F-007-first-class-sandbox.md). These are different safeguards; together they **have not yet established this broader user-control outcome**.
gaps.missingMarkdown: The user's authority over agent/tool actions, data access, external effects, concurrent editing and reversibility has not been proven coherently across representative real workflows. This is about **permissions, consent and control**, distinct from application installation/recovery (F-001) or whether a creative task produces the right result (F-003).
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: Representative real workflows show clear and enforceable grant/deny/revoke permissions, correctly scoped file/network/spend access, handling of concurrent edits, inspectable changes, refusal and undo/recovery after failed or conflicting operations. Isolated execution has its own bounded closure test under F-007; passing it alone does not close this broader gap.

gaps.title: Creative execution isn't yet dependable end to end
gaps.assessmentDetail: Open / foundations exist (2026-11-06).
gaps.desiredMarkdown: From a declared supported, usable Astrid workspace, a creator and agent can choose a creative operation, prepare an appropriate model or provider, execute real inference or media processing, and receive the intended **correct, editable creative result** with progress and recoverable failures. The core proof is successful creative work—not reinstalling or updating Astrid.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Astrid has Runtime execution/task primitives, packs, generation integrations and the video editor. [Plan 02](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/plans/02-consistent-generation/plan.md) aims to establish consistent defaults and pinned stack on fixtures and a fresh Linux CPU setup, **explicitly not real inference**. [Plan 12](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/plans/12-multiple-inference-routes/plan.md) targets real multiple inference routes. [Plan 20](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/plans/20-zero-to-first-image/plan.md) targets a real first generated image on a timeline; [Plan 16](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/plans/16-streamlined-agent-experience/plan.md) improves agent readiness.
gaps.missingMarkdown: The end-to-end **creative job**—capability selection, model/provider readiness, actual task execution, artifact identity and usable output—has not been dependably proven across selected supported workflows and failure paths. Install/update lifecycle belongs to F-001; approval and access decisions belong to F-002.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: On a stated supported setup, run real creative generation or processing and inspect the resulting editable artifact for correct content, project identity, output settings and usable timeline/workspace integration. Demonstrate failed-job diagnostics, stop/retry and cleanup; separately qualify platform installation and permission boundaries in F-001/F-002.

gaps.title: Pack installation and upgrades aren't yet proven under demanding conditions
gaps.assessmentDetail: Open / partial current mechanisms (2026-11-06).
gaps.desiredMarkdown: Demanding packs that meet the [live, portable extension contract](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/vision/pillars/liquid-software.md#packs-are-live-portable-and-extensible) can be installed, enabled, used, updated, disabled and safely rolled back with their frontend and backend contributions intact. Compatibility, source identity, trust, ownership and project-reference continuity remain understandable and reliable through failures and recovery.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Agent has manifest-defined packs with actions, skills, UI and rendering contributions. App has trusted bundled extension lifecycle and editor SDK mechanisms. [Plan 06](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/plans/06-packs/plan.md) explicitly targets pack extraction and reliable installation, trust, transaction, rendering and editor integration. [Plan 11](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/plans/11-threejs-pack/plan.md) is a case of converting a first-party feature into a pack, but is not a generic workspace engine.
gaps.missingMarkdown: We haven't tested a diverse set of demanding frontend, backend and combined packs far enough to expose the limits of the extension system. Installation, real use, upgrade, rollback and recovery need integrated, version-pinned proof across dependency, compatibility, trust, failure and project-state boundaries.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: Run meaningful frontend-only, backend-only and combined packs against real project data, including substantial interactive UI and long-running processing. Demonstrate install, use, update and rollback with pinned source identity; include dependency conflicts, rejected/untrusted contributions, incompatible versions, failed migrations, interruption and recovery without lost project references. Do not claim arbitrary dynamically generated third-party code can run safely without independent isolation evidence.

gaps.title: Local-first projects can't yet use cloud execution seamlessly
gaps.assessmentDetail: Open; remote routes exist but an integrated cloud-assisted local-files workflow has not been qualified.
gaps.desiredMarkdown: A creator keeps **the Astrid project database and durable files on their own machine**, while consenting to an optional cloud agent session, remote image/video generation and remote video rendering. The agent handles provider selection, setup and execution within approved permissions and budgets; inputs sent to remote services are explicit and scoped. Results come back as correct editable files/operations in the same local workspace, with progress, cancellation, retry, recoverability and cleanup.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Astrid Agent has local orchestration and selected provider/RunPod generation routes; [documented execution paths](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-agent/blob/main/docs/reference/where-things-run.md) distinguish provider APIs from local and RunPod inference. [Reigh Worker Orchestrator](https://github.com/banodoco/reigh-worker-orchestrator) documents RunPod worker and fal/Wavespeed API orchestration, but [the satellite-disposition review](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-agent/blob/main/tools/astrid-rename/satellites.md) marks that repository deprecated, with current deployment unverified. None of this establishes **an end-to-end Astrid cloud-agent + generation + render product** retaining local file/database authority.
gaps.missingMarkdown: Creators do not yet have a qualified, coherent way to delegate approved work from a locally owned Astrid project to cloud compute and return to that same editable project with clear consent, costs and recovery. The missing outcome is the reliable boundary between local custody and remote work—not a specific cloud provider, agent API or rendering service.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: With one approved provider/configuration and a declared local project, a user or their agent launches remote work (including image generation and a video render), watches status and costs, cancels/retries as appropriate, and receives correctly linked editable local artifacts with the **local database still authoritative**. A qualification report covers data actually transmitted, permissions, cleanup, non-success paths, security boundaries and retention. Offline/unsupported cases are identified honestly.

gaps.title: Creators can't yet work in Astrid entirely from the cloud
gaps.assessmentDetail: Open; no qualified fully hosted project/database/media lifecycle.
gaps.desiredMarkdown: A creator can use Astrid from a browser without maintaining a local install. The hosted workspace owns persistent project/database state, files/media, accounts and access controls, while cloud agents, generation and video rendering execute under explicit authorization and clear budgets. Projects can be exported or migrated back into user custody; reliable backup, restore, isolation and deletion are supported.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Astrid has a browser-capable App, Runtime and cloud/provider execution paths, but the [Cloud-assisted V1 plan](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/plans/25-cloud-assist-v1/plan.md) deliberately **keeps durable files and project database local**. An always-available hosted tenancy, canonical cloud database, durable object storage and migration/recovery contract are not qualified.
gaps.missingMarkdown: There is no qualified way to start a creative project, keep its working state and files, and return to it in a browser without maintaining a local Astrid install. Durable, account-scoped access, recovery and export are part of that user outcome; the particular database, storage and hosting architecture are choices for implementing it, not the definition of the gap.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: A new user can open a hosted Astrid workspace in a browser, create a project, save and reopen across sessions/devices, run a generation and render, and observe durable, permission-scoped data; accounts are isolated. Backup/restore, quota, delete, export/migration and interrupted execution are tested. A local-first/offline option remains a distinct supported route rather than being silently replaced.

gaps.title: Running Astrid in a sandbox isn't yet a first-class option
gaps.assessmentDetail: Open; sandbox foundations exist, but an integrated, qualified user-facing full-stack path has not been demonstrated (2026-11-07).
gaps.desiredMarkdown: People can choose to run Astrid's creative environment—App, Agent, Runtime and permitted tools—in an isolated sandbox as a normal, understandable setup option. They can grant and revoke access to host files, credentials, network destinations, external inference services and compute resources without needing to manage low-level containment themselves. They can work, stop and recover predictably, and understand any integrations that cross the isolation boundary.
gaps.currentMarkdown: There is relevant ongoing work: [Astrid Agent PR #109](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-agent/pull/109) contains OpenShell sandbox setup and controls, and [Plan 15](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/plans/15-openshell-safe-execution/plan.md) covers an integrated full-stack option. Current Agent sources include sandbox scripts, but their existence does not demonstrate a supported, first-class end-to-end user experience or verified isolation across the App, Agent and Runtime. The PR was open when checked on 2026-11-07; environment and platform qualification remain to be established.
gaps.missingMarkdown: There is no proven, user-friendly path for selecting, starting and using a **fully isolated Astrid workspace** with understandable permissions and boundaries. The outcome is independent of a particular sandbox technology: OpenShell is one possible implementation, not the definition of the gap.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: On a declared supported platform, a user can choose the sandbox mode, start the required stack, perform an approved creative job, stop and restart, and recover their project. Show positive and negative checks for permissions to host files/credentials, network and external inference, including denied actions, cancellation and safe teardown. Document what runs inside versus outside, any opted-in host integration, and residual risks. This proves a bounded supported isolation option, not universal security or a complete answer to [the broader user-control gap F-002](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/vision/gaps/F-002-safe-user-control.md).

gaps.title: Generation isn't yet one portable, extensible path across machines and inference engines
gaps.assessmentDetail: Open; path review and live RunPod attempts (2026-11-08).
gaps.desiredMarkdown:
The [generation aspiration](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/vision/principles/eliminate-needless-technical-wrangling.md#one-generation-path-any-engine-any-machine) is proven for every supported slot, including composed workflows such as h3_av, across local GPUs, a user's server and rented machines. Requests declare custom-node and model requirements and support align, check and trust modes; results return to the creator.

ComfyUI through VibeComfy is the first engine, with Wan2GP providing the second-engine proof. Rented machines can be reused while warm and retain models on attached storage, so a second job does not download them again. A new workflow, engine or provider meets its declared contract without a new route through Astrid's core.
gaps.currentMarkdown:
- **On RunPod, live attempts on 7–8 Nov 2026 produced image and edit; voice and music did not produce an output.**
  - Placement is re-decided in several places.
  - A rented pod is driven as a remote ComfyUI, so checks ran against the controller's disk.
  - Every fresh pod downloads one fixed 95.8 GB model bundle, whatever the job.
  - Pods can't be reused across jobs, and the storage volume is used only off the main path.
- **Some slots don't follow the common path.**
  - Sound effects is refused on RunPod.
  - h3_av has its own pod route.
  - About 50 sites branch by modality.
- **Building blocks exist but are not on one path.** VibeComfy already offers requirements, node install, model fetch and run commands that the Agent partly duplicates.
- **Only one engine works.** Wan2GP is a stub.

The evidence is the merge-run path review in `banodoco/astrid-overnight-2026-11-05`, branch `merge-run/2026-11-07`, `merge-run/path-review/` (VISION, HOLISTIC, EXISTING-MACHINERY and the audits).
gaps.missingMarkdown: There is no single, engine-neutral generation path whose placement is decided once, and its levels (workflows, engines, machines) can't yet be extended independently. Creators can't freely choose and change where a generation runs, or which inference engine runs it, and get the same behaviour, setup and result every time. Distinct from [F-003](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/vision/gaps/F-003-creative-execution.md), which is about one creative job being dependable end to end on a stated setup, and from [F-005](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/vision/gaps/F-005-local-files-cloud-assist.md), which is about the local-data and cloud-execution product boundary.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown:
**Same request, different machines.** The same generation request, for every default slot plus h3_av, produces its result through the same code path on:
- a local GPU;
- a user's own ComfyUI;
- a rented RunPod machine.

**Placement is one decision.** A default placement is set and overridden for a single generation.

**Rented machines are efficient.**
- A second job reuses a warm machine.
- Models already on attached storage are not downloaded again.
- Align, check and trust behave the same everywhere.

**Each level extends independently.**
- A second inference engine (Wan2GP) runs a generation through the same placement, lease and machine route, adding only its own setup and run step.
- A workflow added as a VibeComfy plugin (h3_av) runs with no plugin-specific code in Astrid's core.
- A further kind of machine or provider can be added behind the same placement and lease contract, shown at least with a test provider, without changing the path.

**One path in the code.** Source inspection shows one placement decision site, one submit and one retrieve, and no per-modality branch on the path.

**Negative cases:** a missing model fails before submit, naming the machine; an expired lease releases the machine; no orphaned machine remains.

gaps.title: Creative components can't yet move freely
gaps.assessmentDetail: Open, source inspection (2026-11-06).
gaps.desiredMarkdown: Real creative components (timeline, player, inspector, gallery and others) can move, dock, resize, float and nest within a declarative workspace without losing their state, supported behavior or resource bindings.
gaps.currentMarkdown: The [App source map](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/plans/24-liquid-workspace/inputs.md) identifies actual reusable editor views and a custom two-pane assembly. The standard editor shell still includes host-specific layout, gesture and context responsibilities. **This does not establish a general-purpose portable workspace host.**
gaps.missingMarkdown: Component definitions, instances, presentation lifecycle, resizing and positioning are not yet proven independently portable across workspace layouts and creative domains. Responsive behavior and stable state during docking, nesting and container resizing are essential parts of this gap.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: Rearrange the **real** player, inspector and timeline; retain playback, editing, selection and recovery state; save/restore the layout. Then host a genuinely different domain component using the same contract, without modifying the main editor shell.

gaps.title: Agents can't yet reconfigure the workspace
gaps.assessmentDetail: Open, source inspection (2026-11-06).
gaps.desiredMarkdown: An agent and a person use the same supported workspace operations to open, place, attach, bind, focus and restore component instances. Changes are inspectable, scoped, reversible and compatible with live creative work.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Astrid Agent has pack/skill/action discovery. Astrid App has extensions, commands and scoped editing contexts. The [source review](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/plans/24-liquid-workspace/inputs.md) has **not** established a public, domain-neutral workspace manipulation API.
gaps.missingMarkdown: Spatial **placement/attachment** and functional **resource binding** need explicit, validated operations; proximity alone must not silently connect data. Agents should compose existing software without generating frontend code for ordinary layout changes.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: An agent arranges the same real components as a user, binds the correct timeline/selection/clock, offers reversible operations, does not clobber user edits, and restores a prior workspace from a saved representation.

gaps.title: Frontend and backend extensions don't yet compose
gaps.assessmentDetail: Open, source inspection (2026-11-06).
gaps.desiredMarkdown: A creator or agent can discover and use one pack's creative capability, its typed results and its appropriate frontend components together—extending opinionated tools without bespoke, duplicate integrations.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Astrid Agent pack manifests can declare actions, UI, renderers and skills. Astrid App has a video-editor extension SDK, typed data lanes, proposals and rendering hooks. Current pack UI hosting is still tied to supported host entries; **general component-owned extension points and unified live composition are unproven**.
gaps.missingMarkdown: Common identity and discovery across pack contributions, semantic resource/result bindings, component-defined extension hosts and safe activation need proving beyond the default video editor.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: An installed/trusted music capability yields a typed beat-grid result used in a real timeline view and music control surface. The interface can be rearranged, results correctly track source-to-timeline coordinates, and updates follow existing authoritative domain editing/undo. A second distinct extension domain validates generality.

gaps.title: A creative ecosystem across modalities isn't yet established
gaps.assessmentDetail: Open; vision and draft-plan assessment (2026-11-07), not a qualification of current product coverage.
gaps.desiredMarkdown: Astrid grows into an open ecosystem of powerful, agent-native, deeply extensible creative foundations across video, images, music, 3D and further modalities. The collective and independent contributors can create, publish, adapt and maintain these foundations; other people and agents can build additional tools and capabilities on top of them, combine them and make ambitious work without forking Astrid's core. Video is a deliberate starting point, not a limit on the underlying philosophy.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Astrid is primarily a video editor and timeline, with generation, packs, agent protocols and supporting capabilities. We do not yet offer comparably powerful, extensible image, 3D or writing editors as reusable foundations. Video is an exciting starting point, but not the limit of the ambition. [Packs](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/plans/06-packs/plan.md), [VibeComfy extensibility](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/plans/17-vibecomfy-extensibility/plan.md), [timeline foundations](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/plans/18-timeline-editing/plan.md), [Three.js extraction](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/plans/11-threejs-pack/plan.md) and [liquid workspaces](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/plans/24-liquid-workspace/plan.md) are related implementation directions, not evidence of a flourishing cross-modal ecosystem.
gaps.missingMarkdown: It is not yet demonstrated that people can establish and share **reusable modality-level foundations** beyond video, or that independent contributors can build on those foundations to create further creative tools. This is broader than [LS-003](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/vision/gaps/LS-003-full-stack-contributions.md), which concerns composable frontend/backend extension contracts within a working host; it is also distinct from proving one artist's end-to-end workflow under [AA-001](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/vision/gaps/AA-001-sustained-creative-work.md).
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: On documented supported setups, creators and agents successfully make real work using video plus at least two non-video modality foundations, with preserved files and project control. At least one non-video foundation is contributed outside the core team, and another independent contributor can build and publish a useful additional capability on top of it without a bespoke core fork. Show actual creative results; discoverability, setup, shared agent/user interfaces, extension and update paths, permissions, recovery and meaningful negative cases; and feedback from creators who use these tools. This demonstrates a reusable cross-modal ecosystem, **not** a claim that every imaginable modality has been completed.

gaps.title: Agents can't yet reliably create and maintain their own tools
gaps.assessmentDetail: Open; initial assessment (2026-11-10); not implementation proof.
gaps.desiredMarkdown: An agent can build or adapt a needed tool during creative work, register it with supported interfaces, keep it working as dependencies evolve and make every consequential change inspectable, permissioned and reversible.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Astrid has packs, agent skills and extension points, and [Plan 06](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/plans/06-packs/plan.md) covers a trusted pack lifecycle. There is not yet reliable proof of an agent creating a tool, testing it against real creative work and maintaining it through later updates. Source/plan reassessment, 26 November 2026: [Plan 78](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/plans/78-live-custom-element-editing/plan.md) defines live agent-written custom rendering element admission, exact revision pins and no editor reload, under its explicitly trusted local project-pack assumption. That is meaningful prior art, not proof of an agent authoring, replacing and maintaining a complete interactive tool or of isolation for untrusted contributions. [Plan 41's draft refinement](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/plans/41-agent-managed-tools/plan.md) targets this missing evidence; no new product qualification is claimed.
gaps.missingMarkdown: Agent-led authoring, verification, registration, compatibility monitoring, repair and rollback are not a unified proven flow. Installing or upgrading someone else's existing pack under [F-004](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-dev/blob/21feb35007210df7bc23a03c6226e2c5873fdab1/vision/gaps/F-004-pack-lifecycle.md) does not establish this capability.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown: For a real creative task, an agent creates or adapts a narrow tool, tests it, shows its source and permissions, and requests approval to activate it. On a later breaking dependency change, it proposes a tested repair and can revert safely. Broken, malicious and incompatible cases do not lose work or acquire execution rights.

gaps.title: The creative foundation is not yet independent of its clients and creative environments
gaps.assessmentDetail: Open; source-observed implementation coupling, 2026-11-26; product journey not yet qualified.
gaps.desiredMarkdown: A creator can open, inspect, edit and preserve the same authoritative workspace through a browser, local application, CLI or independent agent, without the foundation depending on any particular interface, agent provider or creative-language environment. When a managed environment or agent breaks, the creator can still access their work, see what happened, repair or replace the failed component and continue unrelated work. Independent contributors can implement a client or capability against documented contracts without importing the core's private implementation, with consistent editing semantics and permission boundaries.
gaps.currentMarkdown: Observed in source reviewed 2026-11-26 (the published-main source identities are historical observations, not release qualification): the [Runtime protocol](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-runtime/blob/686ca695469bda48cd40a70824c4ccef2a137284/contract/README.md) already defines generated clients, authoritative tasks, state, idempotency and version checks. However, the [Agent generic host](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-agent/blob/dc45d97c6bc2734cbfb9b2a25b43cb40ed5757e5/astrid/core/execution/generic_host.py) imports Runtime implementation modules; the [Runtime timeline provider](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-runtime/blob/686ca695469bda48cd40a70824c4ccef2a137284/runtime_protocol/timeline_commit_provider.py) dynamically imports a synchronous Python authoring provider. The [bootstrap](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-app/blob/cc1d48f016fde55ad6b0609c619d8a4bcec56823/public/install) provisions Python before the installer can run; the [Agent installer](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-agent/blob/dc45d97c6bc2734cbfb9b2a25b43cb40ed5757e5/astrid/installer/runtime_lifecycle.py) and [App development launcher](https://github.com/banodoco/astrid-app/blob/cc1d48f016fde55ad6b0609c619d8a4bcec56823/scripts/dev-local-workspace.mjs) share lifecycle responsibilities with Runtime. The current Python Runtime is itself dependent on an interpreter; its pyproject also declares schema-validation dependencies. This is positive evidence of architectural dependence, not evidence that every supported current journey fails. Existing release branches may already resolve some of the reported duplication; re-inventory before code.
gaps.missingMarkdown: The foundation cannot yet be independently started, operated and recovered with the same creative semantics while replaceable client, provider or managed-language environments are absent, failed or independently implemented. F-001 measures the reliability of supported installation transitions, F-004 pack lifecycle, LS-003 frontend/backend extension composition and LS-004 modality ecosystem breadth; those can improve without establishing an independent core, and this gap can close without qualifying every pack, GPU, modality or hosted service.
gaps.closureEvidenceMarkdown:
- E1 — A separately implemented client and worker use documented, versioned contracts without private implementation imports, and read the same project and task receipts as the supported SDKs; unknown versions, stale writes and unauthorized operations are refused.
- E2 — On declared Windows, Linux and macOS installations, the same workspace is accessible through the supported hosted and bundled local React interfaces, native shell and CLI. After intentionally breaking the managed Python or Node environment, the native recovery path diagnoses and repairs it without losing work or creating a second owner. External managers are respected; offline local editing does not need the hosted site.
- E3 — The same edit command corpus from Python, TypeScript and browser preview yields equivalent timeline semantics, with canonical commits, history, rendering inputs and undo preserved. Concurrent incompatible edits, stale head, invalid commands and crash/retry have documented outcomes; a preview cannot bypass commit authority.
- E4 — A native, headless workspace starts and reads/edits existing projects, handles state, media and task admission without Python, Node, an agent or UI. A verified migration preserves data and provenance; interrupted writes, backup/restore, rollback eligibility, permissions and duplicate-owner refusal are exercised.
- E5 — An agent provider is killed or replaced during a real creative task: already admitted work continues or safely settles, the next authorized agent resumes from inspectable durable context/receipts, and unrelated work is unaffected. No provider-private reasoning or credentials are silently transferred.
- E6 — The same versioned core and task/worker contract work in local and isolated headless remote deployments. The same capability executes with explicit placement and scoped inputs; disconnect, retry and revoke preserve custody, avoid duplicate settlement and do not silently spend or upload. Fully hosted account service and all cloud routes remain separate outcomes.

projects.title: One update path and release
projects.goalMarkdown: One working way to update: Update now or Update in Pinokio, with every screen agreeing, and a release number that changes only when what users install changes.

projects.title: Zero-to-first-image onboarding
projects.goalMarkdown: One onboarding skill, named at every install entry point (the Agent README and the App's install briefs), takes a person or their agent from the install line to a generated image on the timeline.
